title: 2020年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Three children in every classroom have a diagnosable mental health condition. Half of these are behavioural disorders, while one third are emotional disorders such as stress, anxiety and depression, which often become outwardly apparent through self-harm. There was an astonishing 52 percent jump in hospital admissions for children and young people who had harmed themselves between 2009 and 2015.

P2 Schools and teachers have consistently reported the scale of the problem since 2009. Last year, over half of teachers reported that more of their pupils experience mental health problems than in the past. But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs,

P3 Part of the reason for the increased pressure on schools is that there are now fewer 'early intervention(干预)' and low-level mental health services based in the community. Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line.

P4 The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools.

P5 There are strong arguments for why schools are best placed to provide mental health services. Schools see young people more than any other service, which gives them a unique ability to get to hard- to-reach children and young people and build meaningful relationships with them over time. Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment. Young people have reported that for low-level conditions such as stress and anxiety, a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting(令人却步的).

P6 There are already examples of innovative schools which combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum. This will, though, require a huge cultural shift. Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services.

options: There are too many students requiring special attention.
They are under too much stress counselling needy students.
Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention.
They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What are teachers complaining about? 用 what 直接问一个客观事实，没有 infer/suggest/imply 之类的推断信号词。 46. What are teachers complaining about? A) There are too many students requiring special attention. B) They are under too much stress counselling needy students. C) Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention. D) They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems.

【拆句】题干 What are teachers complaining about? 是现在进行时的特殊疑问句，主语 teachers、谓语 are complaining about，介词 about 后被前置疑问词 what 取代，无从 句、无否定，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs, and often cite a lack of training, expertise and support from the National Health Service(英国国家医疗服务体系). 但是教师们也一贯反映自己在应对学生心理健康需求时装备多么不足，并经常列举培训、专 业能力和来自英国国家医疗服务体系支持的缺乏。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 There are too many students requiring special attention. 把抱怨内容偷换成学生数 量过多，但原文 a lack of training, expertise and support 抱怨的是教师自身资源不 足，并未说学生人数太多。 B) 偷换概念 They are under too much stress counselling needy students. 把抱怨内容换成教师 承受过大压力，但原文 how ill-equipped they feel 抱怨的是装备不足，不是工作压 力大。 C) 以偏概全 Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention. 用 any intervention（任何干预）把范围放大；原文只说教师在应对心理需求上装备不足，并 未说学校不能实施任何干预。 D) ✓ 正确 a lack of training, expertise and support ↔lack the necessary resources to meet pupils' mental health needs ↔to address pupils' mental problems 预判的两个语义点（缺资源、为了应对学生心理问题）都精确落在 They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems. 里，故锁定。 从文章中我们对英国社区卫生服务了解到什么? A) 由于预算削减,它们已经恶化。 B) 它们为当地居民的日常生活提供便利。 C) 它们在帮助精神病患者方面被证明无效。 D) 它们为当地居民提供预防性护理。

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain?
options: They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.
They facilitate local residents' everyday lives.
They prove ineffective in helping mental patients.
They cover preventative care for the local resident.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain? 中 learn from the passage 是定向取信息，不是推断，问的是文中已陈述的事实。 47. What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain? A) They have deteriorated due to budget cuts. B) They facilitate local residents' everyday lives. C) They prove ineffective in helping mental patients. D) They cover preventative care for the local resident.

【拆句】题干结构为 What + do we learn + from the passage + about + community health services in Britain；about 短语限定要问的对象，in Britain 进一步限定地域。理解时 把 What do we learn 视作信息询问的固定外壳，重心放在 about 后面那串名词短语，无 陷阱。

【定位】Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line. 自 2010 年以来对地方财政预算的削减导致了这些服务的大幅衰退，尽管有强有力的证据证 明它们在预防后续危机方面的有效性。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services ↔They have deteriorated due to budget cuts. a significant decline of these services ↔They have deteriorated 预判的两个要点（衰退 + 预算削减为因）都精确落在 They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.，且因果方向一致，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 They facilitate local residents' everyday lives. 说社区服务便利居民日常生活，但原文 从未谈到对日常生活的便利，只谈预算与衰退。 C) 与原文相反 They prove ineffective in helping mental patients. 说服务被证明无效，但原文 strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line 明确说有强证据证明其有效——正反相反。 D) 偷换概念 They cover preventative care for the local resident. 看似呼应 preventing crises， 但 preventative care 通常指预防性医疗保健，与原文 preventing crises further down the line（预防后续危机）不是一回事；且本题问的是文章对社区服务的描述要 点，原文重点是衰退，不是预防覆盖。 作者建议将心理健康服务设置在哪里? A) 在家里。 B) 在学校。 C) 在医院。 D) 在社区。

questions.q: Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed?
options: At home.
At school.
In hospitals.
In communities.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 用 where 直 问地点，配 suggest 提示要找作者明确写出的建议位置，仍是文章里已有的事实陈述。 48. Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? A) At home. B) At school. C) In hospitals. D) In communities.

【拆句】题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 表层是特殊疑 问句，深层是 suggest + that 从句的虚拟语气结构——从句省略了 that，谓语用 (should) be placed 的原形被动，should 被省略。基础薄弱考生易把 be placed 误读成时态错误， 其实是 suggest 后建议性虚拟。

【定位】The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools. 打破心理健康服务和学校双方压力的唯一办法是把早期干预服务重新投入到学校之内。

【选项】A) 无中生有 At home. 在家中提供，原文 inside schools 与 Schools see young people more than any other service 反复强调学校，从未提到在家中提供心理服务。 B) ✓ 正确 inside schools ↔At school. 预判要求的地点是学校内部，四个选项里只有 At school. 对应，故锁定。 C) 与原文相反 In hospitals. 与原文 a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting 的态度相反—— 作者把医院/诊所环境视为令人却步的，反对在医院里提供低强度服务。 D) 张冠李戴 In communities. 看似呼应 low-level mental health services based in the community，但作者讲的是社区服务因预算削减已衰退（Cuts to local authority budgets… have resulted in a significant decline），主张方向已转向学校内部，不是 继续放在社区。 我们从最近的研究中了解到什么? A) 学生更愿意依靠同龄人来缓解压力和焦虑。 B) 年轻人热衷于建立有意义的关系。 C) 学生在学校寻求咨询时感到更自在。 D) 年轻人从各种户外活动中受益。

questions.q: What do we learn from the recent studies?
options: Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety.
Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships.
Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.
Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同句型，问的是研究直接给出的 结论，不需要跨句推断。

【拆句】题干 What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同构，只是把 the passage 换成 the recent studies，结构无陷阱。 49. What do we learn from the recent studies? A) Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety. B) Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships. C) Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school. D) Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities.

【定位】Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment. 近期研究表明，儿童和年轻人在很大程度上更愿意在学校里见心理咨询师，而不愿在校外环 境中见。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety. 称学生倾向于靠同 龄人缓解压力焦虑，但研究结论是关于咨询地点（校内 vs 校外），从未谈到同伴这一 路径。 B) 张冠李戴 Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships. 与 build meaningful relationships with them over time 关键词重合，但原文中这句话的主语 是 Schools/them（即提供方），不是青少年自己；且本题问 recent studies 的结论， 而不是这句一般性描述。 C) ✓ 正确 prefer to see a counsellor in school ↔more comfortable seeking counselling in school children and young people ↔Students 预判的两个要点（学生群体 + 校内更愿）都精确落在 Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities. 谈户外活动的益 处，原文未出现 outdoor activities 这一概念。 作者所说的文化转变(第6段第2行)是什么意思? A) 学校学术课程的简化。 B) 家长参与学校的决策制定。 C) 教师对心理健康态度的转变。 D) 对学校概念的转变。

questions.q: What does the author mean by a cultural shift (Line 2, Para. 6)?
options: Simplification of schools' academic curriculums.
Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making.
A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health.
A change in the conception of what schools are.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 用 What does … mean by … 这一 固定句型直问引文含义，是典型的词义句意题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 是特殊疑问句，主干为 What does the author mean，介词短语 by a cultural shift 引出被询问的短语，注意 mean by 在此 是固定搭配（凭 X 意指什么），后跟括号注明的行号定位。 50. What does the author mean by a cultural shift (Line 2, Para. 6)? A) Simplification of schools' academic curriculums. B) Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making. C) A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health. D) A change in the conception of what schools are.

【定位】Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services. 政界、决策者、采购者和校领导必须有足够的勇气，迈出那一步，把学校重新想象成既提供 健康服务、也提供教育服务的场所。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Simplification of schools' academic curriculums. 简化学术课程，原文 combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum 强调学 术课程要保持坚实，不是简化。 B) 无中生有 Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making. 家长参与学校决策——原文呼吁的 参与者是 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders，并不包含 家长，且谈的不是决策参与而是学校角色重塑。 C) 以偏概全 A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health. 把转变的范围缩窄到教师态度，但 原文 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders 列出的转变主体 不是教师，而是政界、决策者、采购者和校领导——主体错位、范围缩小。 D) ✓ 正确 reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services ↔ A change in the conception of what schools are. 预判的核心（重新定义学校是什么）与 D 的措辞一对一对齐，且 D 的 conception 一词 正好对应 cultural shift 中的 cultural（观念层面的）。
